extracted.intended_audience: exchange listing officials, SRO filing authors, SEC staff, market participants and commenters interested in listing Commodity-Based Trust Shares
extracted.subtask_short: listing rule change for commodity-based trust shares
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and justify a proposed exchange rule change to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares (an exchange-traded product backed by ETH) under the standards of the Securities Exchange Act, including demonstrating surveillance, investor protections, and information transparency. The page is an SEC notice describing the standards and evidence an exchange must present and the disclosures the exchange will make to members and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must determine that the proposal is consistent with the requirements of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, specifically including: (i) the requirement that a national securities exchange's rules are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices; and (ii) the requirement that an exchange proposal be designed, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing should explain how the proposal is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement (SSA) with a regulated market of significant size
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to meet the standard in a proposal to list and trade a series of Commodity-Based Trust Shares, the Commission requires that an exchange demonstrate that there is a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement in place with a regulated market of significant size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common membership in ISG or a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement with a regulated derivatives market (e.g., CME) has been treated as satisfying this requirement. Where an SSA is not present, the exchange may show that other means to prevent fraud and manipulation are sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'significant market' / 'market of significant size' (two-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms “significant market” and “market of significant size” include a market (or group of markets) as to which: (a) there is a reasonable likelihood that a person attempting to manipulate the ETP would also have to trade on that market to manipulate the ETP, so that a surveillance-sharing agreement would assist the listing exchange in detecting and deterring misconduct; and (b) it is unlikely that trading in the ETP would be the predominant influence on prices in that market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing should address both prongs explicitly: (a) whether manipulation of the ETP would reasonably require trading in the referenced regulated market such that SSA data would help detect/deter misconduct, and (b) whether ETP trading is unlikely to be the predominant force driving prices in the referenced market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of alternative means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has recognized that the 'regulated market of significant size' standard is not the only means for satisfying Section 6(b)(5); a listing exchange could demonstrate that 'other means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices' are sufficient to justify dispensing with the requisite surveillance-sharing agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing should describe the alternative measures the exchange will take (e.g., bilateral surveillance-sharing agreements with major spot venues, enhanced surveillance procedures) and provide supporting evidence that those measures are likely to detect and deter fraud and manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence that an underlying regulated market is of 'significant size' (acceptable metrics/evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrating that a derivatives market represents a regulated market of significant size may be supported by metrics and facts such as high correlation between spot and futures prices, futures trading volume and dollar value, number of contracts traded, open interest, number of large open-interest holders, and growth in unique accounts trading the futures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange used examples (e.g., daily correlation between spot ETH and CME ETH Futures of 0.998; monthly contract volumes and dollar values; increases in large open interest holders and unique accounts) to show the CME ETH Futures market is a regulated market of significant size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration that manipulation of the ETP would implicate the regulated futures market (manipulation link/prong (a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that there is a reasonable likelihood that a person attempting to manipulate the ETP would also have to trade on the regulated futures market to manipulate the ETP, so that a surveillance-sharing agreement would assist in detecting and deterring misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing cites precedent (e.g., Teucrium approval, Bitcoin Futures ETF rationale, and court acknowledgment in Grayscale) and the high correlation between spot and futures pricing to argue that CME surveillance can capture effects on futures caused by trading on spot markets and thus aid in detecting manipulation of an ETP referencing spot ETH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration that the ETP would not be the predominant influence on prices (prong (b): predominant influence analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange and Sponsor should show that trading in the Shares would not be the predominant force on prices in the referenced market (e.g., CME ETH Futures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support may include: the Trust will not hold CME ETH Futures contracts; the Trust would represent a very small percentage of daily spot ETH trading volume (e.g., $9.4B average 24-hour spot volume versus expected Trust size); the spot market is deeper and more liquid than the futures market (court findings such as Grayscale), making manipulation more difficult; and market maturity indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance supplementation via bilateral Spot Crypto SSA (e.g., Coinbase agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where additional surveillance is necessary, the Exchange may enter into a bilateral surveillance-sharing agreement with a major U.S.-based spot trading platform (the 'Spot Crypto SSA') to supplement the Exchange's market surveillance program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Spot Crypto SSA is expected to have the hallmarks of an ISG member SSA, providing supplemental access to data regarding spot ETH trades (orders and trades) and permitting the Exchange to request further information from the spot venue when necessary to detect and investigate potential manipulation in trading of the Commodity-Based Trust Shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Circular disclosures to members prior to trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to commencement of trading, the Exchange will inform its members in an Information Circular of the special characteristics and risks associated with trading the Shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Information Circular must discuss: (i) procedures for creation and redemption of Baskets (and that Shares are not individually redeemable); (ii) BZX Rule 3.7 suitability obligations for members recommending the Shares; (iii) how information regarding the IIV and the Trust's NAV are disseminated; (iv) the risks involved in trading the Shares outside Regular Trading Hours when an updated IIV will not be calculated or publicly disseminated; (v) the requirement that members deliver a prospectus to investors purchasing newly issued Shares prior to or concurrently with confirmation; and (vi) trading information and any exemptive/no-action/interpretive relief from the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospectus delivery obligations for resales
rubrics_metrics.description: Members purchasing the Shares for resale to investors will deliver a prospectus to such investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prospectus must be delivered prior to or concurrently with confirmation of a transaction. The Information Circular will advise members of these prospectus delivery requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing and continued listing criteria under Exchange Rule 14.11(e)(4) and surveillance/delicensing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Shares will be listed pursuant to the initial and continued listing criteria in Exchange Rule 14.11(e)(4); the issuer's statements regarding portfolio description, limits, and applicability of Exchange rules shall constitute continued listing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange must represent that its surveillance procedures are adequate to monitor trading of the Shares during all trading sessions and to deter/detect violations. The issuer must advise the Exchange of any failure to comply with continued listing requirements; the Exchange will surveil under Section 19(g)(1) of the Exchange Act and may commence delisting procedures under Exchange Rule 14.12 if the Trust or Shares are not in compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and transparency of pricing and Trust information (IIV, NAV, holdings, index data)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal should promote market transparency by making a large amount of information available about ETH and the Trust and Shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific transparency expectations: an IIV per Share updated every 15 seconds during Regular Trading Hours (but not a substitute for end-of-day NAV); IIV widely disseminated by major market data vendors and online services; Trust website publicly accessible and containing current NAV per Share (daily) and prior business day's NAV and reported closing price; BZX Official Closing Price in relation to NAV and premium/discount calculation; charts displaying frequency distribution of discounts/premiums for the prior four calendar quarters (or life of Trust); the prospectus and other quantitative information; daily dissemination of the Trust's holdings; ETH price available from major market data vendors updated at least every 15 seconds; information about the Index and key elements of Index calculation publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAV calculation and market data dissemination protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: The NAV for the Trust will be calculated by the Administrator once a day and disseminated daily to all market participants at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation and last-sale information for the Shares will be disseminated through the facilities of the CTA. Quotation and last-sale information for ETH is widely disseminated through major market data vendors (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters) and exchanges; depth-of-book information for ETH is also available from ETH exchanges. Normal trading hours for ETH exchanges are 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulation of investor-protection and public-interest benefits as part of approval justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchange should explain how approving the proposal protects investors and the public interest and how benefits may outweigh manipulation concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange identified quantifiable investor protection issues from OTC ETH Funds and argued approval would (i) reduce premium/discount volatility; (ii) reduce management fees through competition; (iii) reduce risks and costs associated with investing in ETH Futures ETFs and operating companies that are imperfect proxies for ETH exposure; and (iv) provide an alternative to custodying spot ETH.
